section: A zero-shot robot policy asked to produce the end state
setup: pi0.5-DROID runs zero-shot in the same 41 test scenes. A Franka arm replaces the scene's tool, every object, mass and material is unchanged. The policy sees its camera images and an instruction that states the end state of the recorded motion, alone or with the motion described in words. Each scene is attempted twice per instruction; an attempt lasts 30 s.
tile_note: The policy tile is filmed from the recording's camera in the plain look of the policy's simulation (no walls); the PhysX and NeuWorld tiles are the path-traced render of the same scene. NeuWorld is not asked the same question here: its tile is the forward prediction of the recorded action, to show the motion the policy would have to cause.
selection_note: Four attempts picked by hand: a wrong manipulation, two attempts that never touch the object the recording acts on (the most common outcome) and one of the three successes.

table.caption: pi0.5-DROID, zero-shot, on the 41 test scenes (Table 14 of the supplementary). Moved: attempts in which the object the recorded action acts on is moved. Reached: attempts that reach the end state, on the 34 scenes (68 attempts) where it can be reached.
rows: Hold, then let go or throw

items.recorded_action_kind: pushed by a tool in the recording
items.description: Recorded motion: an arm pushes the ball, which knocks the block into the box and follows it in.
items.policy_note: The policy grasps the red ball, lifts it and drops it off the table next to the box; the block never moves.
items.instruction: get the blue block and the red ball into the wooden box on the floor. Masses: ball 0.4 kg, block 0.28 kg.

outcome.meaning: error = summed end-state error of the tracked objects divided by the same sum when nobody acts; reached below 0.5; moved = the acted object ends at least 2 cm farther from its start than with nobody acting
